title: America’s largest newspaper chain, USA Today Co., partners with Palantir to analyze audience data as search traffic falls
excerpt: USA Today Co. has made a deal with software company Palantir to analyze and monetize user behavior, the company announced on Thursday. content_html:
USA Today Co. has made a deal with software company Palantir to analyze and monetize user behavior, the company announced on Thursday.

In its Q2 earnings call Thursday morning, USA Today Co. chairman and CEO Mike Reed told investors he expects the partnership to “strengthen how we collect, connect and activate audience data to drive more effective and faster monetization across our platform.”

“Every visit, every session, and every moment of attention creates a signal,” Reed said. “When we connect those signals, they become actionable intelligence that allows us to engage users more effectively and monetize those relationships faster and at much greater value. The work our team is doing with Palantir is a direct extension of this strategy. We are applying Palantir’s AI-powered platform to one of the largest opportunities in front of us, converting the sheer scale of our audience into known, orchestrated first-party relationships, because that is what turns our reach into sustainable, higher value revenue.”

USA Today Co. owns more than 200 local newspapers in the United States, along with its national daily USA Today. The partnership with Palantir comes as search traffic continues to fall — a challenge faced by publications around the world, and one The New York Times mentioned in its own earnings report Wednesday. USA Today Co. reported 158 million unique visitors in the second quarter of the year, down from 180 million in the first quarter.

This decline “does not reflect lower demand for the content,” said Kristin Roberts, president of USA Today Media. “What it reflects is lower referrals from traditional search because of those consumer discovery changes that we’re seeing and witnessing.”

Palantir has been the subject of controversy in recent months for providing its technology to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the U.S. Department of Defense, and the Israeli military. The company’s co-founder and chairman is Peter Thiel, the billionaire entrepreneur who funded Hulk Hogan’s defamation lawsuit against Gawker, leading to the publication’s ultimate bankruptcy and closure.

USA Today Co. isn’t the only media company to enlist Palantir’s services. Axel Springer — which owns Business Insider, Politico, Bild, and The Telegraph — and Fox News have also partnered with Palantir for its data intelligence tools. Thomson Reuters also supplies data to Palantir, which had been used by ICE, 404 Media reported in March.

“It’s important to note all of our data remains our data,” Reed told investors. “It’s really just leveraging this incredible AI and software that Palantir has to allow us to move so much faster and to be so much smarter with the data we have today. And…take a lot of the anonymous interactions we have today and turn those into known relationships…The more known relationships we have, the more data we create, the more signals we create, the more actionable intelligence we have.”

Roberts told USA Today Co. employees in an email Thursday that the Palantir partnership could result in “better recommendations and offers based on what people actually care about” and “smarter subscription and advertising experiences” for consumers and subscribers.

“USA TODAY Co. complies with applicable data protection and privacy laws and maintains strong standards for data security and governance,” the company said in a statement to Nieman Lab. “We require this of our vendors and partners as well, reflecting our belief that safeguarding protected personal information is essential to our business and the audiences we serve. Our editorial decisions remain independent and are guided by our longstanding journalistic standards and ethics policies.”

Roberts noted that World Cup coverage across USA Today’s network “generated 97 million pageviews, with search driving nearly 65% of that traffic. That reinforces an important point — when content meets a real and urgent need — search still delivers. But we are not building our future on search, even in our strongest categories. Great content still finds an audience, and our opportunity moving forward is to ensure that our distribution tactics keep pace with the way readers and viewers want to consume content in digital spaces.”

“I can see a day where we turn off scraping or making our content available for the [search engine links],” Reed said. “We’re actually more hopeful that we can be proactive with Google in negotiating a fair licensing deal. That would be our preferred path — to have our content appear both in traditional search as well as in AI summaries. But if we have to cut them off and block them in order to get to a deal, then we’ll do that for sure.”

content_html_zh:
今日美国公司 该公司周四宣布，已与软件公司 Palantir 达成协议，分析用户行为并从中获利。

周四上午，《今日美国》公司在第二季度财报电话会议上表示： 董事长兼首席执行官迈克·里德 (Mike Reed) 告诉投资者，他预计此次合作将“加强我们收集、连接和激活受众数据的方式，以推动我们平台上更有效、更快速的货币化。”

“每次访问、每次会议和每一个关注时刻都会产生一个信号，”里德说。 “当我们连接这些信号时，它们就变成了可操作的情报，使我们能够更有效地吸引用户，并更快地以更大的价值将这些关系货币化。 我们团队与 Palantir 所做的工作是这一策略的直接延伸。 我们正在将 Palantir 的人工智能平台应用于我们面前的最大机遇之一，将我们庞大的受众规模转化为已知的、精心策划的第一方关系，因为这就是我们将影响力转化为可持续的、更高价值的收入的原因。”

今日美国公司 在美国拥有 200 多家当地报纸，以及全国性日报《今日美国》。 与 Palantir 的合作正值搜索流量持续下降之际——这是世界各地出版物面临的挑战，《纽约时报》在周三的收益报告中也提到了这一挑战。 今日美国公司 据报道，今年第二季度的独立访客数量为 1.58 亿，低于第一季度的 1.8 亿。

今日美国媒体总裁克里斯汀·罗伯茨表示，这种下降“并不反映对内容的需求下降”。 “这反映出传统搜索的推荐量较低，因为我们看到和见证了消费者发现的变化。”

近几个月来，Palantir 因向移民和海关执法局 (ICE)、美国国防部和以色列军方提供技术而备受争议。 该公司的联合创始人兼董事长是亿万富翁企业家 Peter Thiel，他资助了 Hulk Hogan 对 Gawker 的诽谤诉讼，导致该出版物最终破产和关闭。

今日美国公司 并不是唯一一家使用 Palantir 服务的媒体公司。 Axel Springer（拥有 Business Insider、Politico、Bild 和 The Telegraph）和福克斯新闻也与 Palantir 合作开发其数据智能工具。 据 404 Media 今年 3 月报道，汤森路透还向 ICE 使用的 Palantir 提供数据。

“重要的是要注意我们所有的数据仍然是我们的数据，”里德告诉投资者。 “Palantir 确实利用了这种令人难以置信的人工智能和软件，让我们能够更快地行动，并且对我们今天拥有的数据变得更加智能。 而且......将我们今天进行的大量匿名互动转化为已知的关系......我们拥有的已知关系越多，我们创建的数据越多，我们创建的信号越多，我们拥有的可操作情报就越多。”

罗伯茨告诉《今日美国》公司。 周四，员工在一封电子邮件中表示，Palantir 合作伙伴关系可能会为消费者和订阅者带来“基于人们真正关心的内容的更好推荐和优惠”以及“更智能的订阅和广告体验”。

“《今日美国》公司 遵守适用的数据保护和隐私法，并维持严格的数据安全和治理标准，”该公司在给尼曼实验室的一份声明中表示。 “我们也要求我们的供应商和合作伙伴这样做，这反映了我们的信念：保护受保护的个人信息对于我们的业务和我们服务的受众至关重要。 我们的编辑决定保持独立，并以我们长期的新闻标准和道德政策为指导。”

罗伯茨指出，《今日美国》网络上的世界杯报道“产生了 9700 万次综合浏览量，其中搜索流量占了近 65%。 这强化了一个重要的观点——当内容满足真实而紧迫的需求时——搜索仍然可以提供服务。 但我们的未来并不是建立在搜索之上，即使是在我们最强大的类别中。 优秀的内容仍然能找到受众，我们前进的机会是确保我们的发行策略跟上读者和观众想要在数字空间消费内容的方式。”

“我可以预见有一天我们会关闭抓取或将我们的内容提供给[搜索引擎链接]，”里德说。 “实际上，我们更希望能够积极主动地与谷歌就公平的许可协议进行谈判。 这将是我们的首选路径——让我们的内容同时出现在传统搜索和人工智能摘要中。 但如果我们必须切断并阻止他们才能达成协议，那么我们肯定会这样做。”
